RadioLog 3.0

Modern logging and station management software for radio amateurs.
Includes logbook tools, DX Cluster workflow, RigControl features,
portable mode and operational support utilities.

Developed by EA5YC.

about.credits_text:
For reception and decoding, FT8 Studio uses the external executable jt9.exe from the WSJT-X project, developed by Joe Taylor (K1JT) and contributors under the GNU GPLv3 licence.

RadioLog does not include or distribute that executable. The user must install WSJT-X separately.

RadioLog's operating interface, transmit control and FT8 encoder/modulator are developed independently.

privacy.dialog.body:
RadioLog stores your logbook and program settings locally on your computer. This data is not automatically sent to RadioLog servers.

When you voluntarily use external services such as QRZ.com, eQSL, LoTW, Club Log, HRDLog or HamQTH, the necessary data may be transmitted to those services and is subject to their own terms and privacy policies.

This data is not sold or used for advertising purposes. It will not be shared with third parties either, except where legally required.

To exercise your rights of access, rectification, erasure, or objection regarding this data, you can write to rgpd@radiolog.es.

RadioLog does not include it or open it: it uses it underneath, without a window, only to decode (it gives it the audio of each period and reads the text). JTDX will not do for this: its decoder cannot be used that way. Choose the folder where WSJT-X is installed (the one containing jt9.exe; usually C:\WSJT\wsjtx\bin) or press «Search automatically»: the usual folders and Windows «Installed programs» are checked.
settings.ft8.status_none: No WSJT-X chosen. Press «Search automatically» or «Browse…».
settings.ft8.not_found: WSJT-X was not found on this computer. Install it (it is free) or press «Browse…» to choose its folder.
settings.ft8.browse_title: Choose the WSJT-X folder (the one containing jt9.exe)
ft8.title: FT8 Studio — Decoder
ft8.clock_tip: Compares the PC time with time servers. In FT8 the PC clock must be right (an error of a few seconds at most): use a program that keeps it synchronised. RadioLog only warns; it does not change the time.
ft8.mode_no_freq: The frequency table has no {modo} frequency on {banda}: the radio stays where it is (you can add one in Settings → FT8 Studio).
ft8.mode_tip: FT8 (15 s periods), FT4 (7.5 s, for contests) and JT65 (1-minute periods, very weak signals).
ft8.ft4_rx_only: This mode cannot transmit yet: receive only for now. Switch to FT8 or FT4 to transmit.
ft8.rx_tip: The audio frequency (Hz) you listen at. What is decoded within ±20 Hz of it, and everything carrying your callsign, goes to the «RX frequency» list. You can also pick it by clicking the waterfall.
ft8.depth_tip: How much effort the decoder puts into each period. Fast decodes the obvious; Deep also looks for weak signals (a bit more CPU: it fits easily in the time of one period).
ft8.idle: Stopped. Press Start to listen (or open a one-period recording). A line's colour flags what is new; «*» next to the country = low-confidence decode.
ft8.listening: Listening… the first complete period is decoded when it ends.
ft8.warn_silence: No audio is arriving (total silence). Check the chosen input, the volume and the Windows microphone privacy settings. Remember: the CAT cable only carries frequency and mode; to receive, the radio's audio has to reach the PC (sound interface, or a sound card with a cable to the radio's data connector).
ft8.depth_lowered: Slow decoder ({s} s): depth lowered to {n}
ft8.dt_mean_tip: DT is how much each signal is early or late against your clock. The MEAN DT of the strong signals should be about 0 (between −0.3 and +0.5 s): the other stations are time-synchronised. If it drifts away from that, your clock or the audio is out of sync.
ft8.slow_decoder: The decoder is slower than the periods: the oldest are dropped. Lower the depth.
ft8.autoseq_off: AutoSeq off: it keeps sending what you chose, but the QSO no longer advances by itself.
ft8.tt_pot: Audio output level to the radio (not the radio's power: leave that alone, it moves the ALC). Remembered per band and mode.
settings.ft8.seq.autoseq: AutoSeq: the QSO advances by itself (report, confirmation and 73)
settings.ft8.freq.radio_mode: Radio mode when picking a band
settings.ft8.freq.mode_none: Leave it alone (I set it on the radio)
settings.ft8.freq.mode_data: Set data (DATA-U; USB if the radio has none)
settings.ft8.freq.help: These are the FT8 and FT4 dial frequencies offered by FT8 Studio's “Band” selector: picking one sets the radio to it over CAT. Those marked ★ are the standard ones; you can change any, add your own (e.g. a DXpedition's), delete those you do not use, restore the standard ones, and IMPORT or EXPORT the .qrg file of JTDX / WSJT-X. “Region” limits a frequency to that region (ALL = all). FT2 will be added once verified frequencies exist.
settings.ft8.freq.restore_ask: Go back to the standard frequency table? Your changes are lost (until you press “Save”; “Cancel” recovers them).
settings.ft8.freq.import_ask:

Merge them with the ones you have, or replace the table?
ft8.band_tip: The FT8 working frequencies (edit the table in Settings → FT8 Studio; ★ = standard). Picking one sets the radio to it over CAT, in the digital mode, and clears the lists. If you move the dial by hand, this shows which one you are on.
ft8.tt_band: FT8 band and working frequency: picking one sets the radio to it over CAT.
ft8.band_busy: The band is not changed while transmitting or tuning: stop first.
ft8.band_no_cat: Connect the radio (the “Connect” button above) to change band from here.
ft8.band_fail: The radio did not accept the frequency change. Check CAT in Settings → Radio / CAT.
ft8.wd_stopped: TX watchdog: transmission stopped after {m} min with no action. Press “Transmit” to carry on.
ft8.tune_on: TUNING at {hz} Hz ({s} s). Press “Tune” or “Stop TX” to finish.
ft8.tt_go: Arms the ticked message: it goes out on every chosen turn until “Stop TX” or until the QSO ends.
ft8.tt_stop: Stops the transmission (and Tune) at once, releases PTT and disables automatic sending.
ft8.tt_tune: Transmits an unmodulated carrier on the TX frequency to adjust the antenna tuner (at most the time set in Settings, 30 s). Press again to stop.
ft8.tt_dx: Callsign of the station you call (double-clicking a line of the list fills it in). The “x” clears it.
ft8.tt_rpt: The report you send: what you receive from the other station (-30 to +32 dB).
ft8.tt_turn: Which turn you transmit in: even (:00 and :30) or odd (:15 and :45). Double-click sets the opposite of the other station's. If a strong neighbour is on the band, use its same turn.
ft8.tt_tx_hz: Audio frequency of your transmission (200 to 2900 Hz). Answering on a different frequency from the CQ avoids QRM from other callers.
ft8.tt_eq_rx: When ticked, the TX frequency always follows the RX one.
ft8.tt_rx_hz: Audio frequency you listen on: what falls there (±10 Hz) goes to “Rx Frequency”. Double-clicking a line sets it; with Ctrl, TX too.
ft8.tt_free: Free text of up to 13 characters (letters, digits and + - . / ?).
ft8.tt_wd: TX watchdog (WD): minutes left before transmission is stopped if you do nothing. Any click or key in this window resets it. Change it in Settings → FT8 Studio.
ft8.tt_state: What FT8 Studio is doing now: receiving, transmitting, tuning or stopped.
ft8.tt_copy: Copies what is shown in “Band Activity” to the clipboard.
ft8.tt_use: Passes the chosen callsign to the QSO entry.
ft8.tt_macros: Short free-text messages with variables (^ name, @ DX call, $ my call, & my base call, # report). Edited in Settings → FT8 Studio → Macros.
ft8.macro_bad: The macro “{texto}” is not valid as a free message: {motivo}.
settings.ft8.wanted.beep: Beep when a wanted station appears
settings.ft8.wanted.help: What you want to chase, comma separated: exact callsigns (“3Y0J”), prefixes with an asterisk (“VP8*” = everything starting with VP8), countries (the name in the Country column, in English) and 4-character grids. Those lines are painted in their own colour (change it in “List colours”) and take priority over the new-station alerts; only lines with your callsign and your current QSO beat them.
settings.ft8.list.worked_help: Marks the lines of stations you already have in the log (exact callsign), in the scope you choose: any band, this band or this band and mode. You can see at a glance whom you have not worked yet. Anything with your callsign or your QSO partner’s is never hidden. If you also want them painted in a colour, enable it in “List colours”.
settings.ft8.list.distance: Show distance and bearing next to the country (when its grid is known)

settings.ft8.list.blank: Leave a blank line between one turn and the next
settings.ft8.list.help: Filters only hide lines in the two lists; what is decoded does not change. Anything with your callsign or that of the station you are in QSO with is always shown. Callsigns: comma separated; “BV*” = all starting with BV. Countries: the name as shown in the Country column (in English), comma separated.
settings.ft8.col.qso: Station I am in QSO with
settings.ft8.col.help: Colours of the “Band activity” and “RX frequency” lines. If a line fits several, this priority applies: calling me (red) · in QSO with me (blue) · “Wanted” · new (the alerts above) · already worked (if enabled) · CQ and 73 (light blue, if enabled). Do not give text and background the same colour: it would not be visible.
ft8.tt_log_qso: Saves the QSO with the DX on screen to the log (lets you check the grid and the reports). Normally it is saved by itself when it ends.
ft8.log_no_dx: Enter the DX callsign first (or double-click a station in the list).
settings.ft8.seq.clear_dx: When a QSO ends, clear the DX on screen (ready for the next one)
settings.ft8.seq.skip_grid: Skip the grid: when answering a CQ, start with the report
settings.ft8.seq.skip_grid_help: Normally you answer a CQ with your call and grid and then send the report. With this box the report goes straight away: it saves one turn (useful in contests and with weak DX).
ft8.tt_cq_to: Who your CQ is for (message 6): everyone, “DX” (also everyone), a continent (NA, SA, EU, AS, AF, OC, AN) or JA. Your own targets (“POTA”…) are added in Settings → FT8 Studio.
ft8.cq_not_for_me: “CQ {destino}” from {dx} is not for you (strict directional CQ): it was prepared, but no call is made.
settings.ft8.seq.cq_strict: Strict directional CQ operation: only answer those who fit my directed CQ, and do not call directed CQs that do not include me
settings.ft8.seq.cq_strict_help: With “CQ EU” only Europeans are answered (you are calling that continent only); with “CQ DX” everyone is answered. And double-clicking someone else’s directed CQ only calls if you fit its target (a continent). Targets that cannot be checked (POTA, numbers…) always count.
settings.ft8.macros.vars: Variables: ^ station name (from the log, 7 letters at most) · @ its call · $ my call · & my base call (no prefix or /P) · # report (R# = report with R). 13 characters at most once replaced.
settings.ft8.macros.help: Each macro is an FT8 free message (letters, digits and + - . / ?). In the window, the “Macros” button shows them with the station and report of that moment already replaced; picking one puts it in the free message.
settings.ft8.tx.same_as_rx: The TX frequency always follows the RX one (otherwise they are independent: the usual way)
settings.ft8.tx.wd: TX watchdog: minutes with no action before stopping
settings.ft8.tx.help: TX watchdog (“WD” in the status bar): if you are transmitting and touch nothing in the window for these minutes, transmission stops by itself (in case you walk away and forget to disable it). Any click or key in the window resets it. “Tune” sends an unmodulated carrier to adjust the antenna tuner and stops by itself at the maximum time.
ft8.clear_list_tip: Erases only this list (also: right-click, or Del for the selected line).
settings.field.update_auto_tip: When a new version is available, RadioLog downloads it in the background and checks that it is intact. Then it shows a button to install it: it never closes or installs by itself. If you untick it, it only notifies and downloads when you ask.
settings.field.clock_fix_tip: If Windows' clock is off, RadioLog adds what the time servers (internet) measure to the on-screen clocks, to the time of every QSO it logs and to FT8 turns, WITHOUT touching Windows' clock and without installing anything. With no internet it uses the PC's time. Untick it if you already sync Windows with another program.

ft8.clock_corrected_tip: Windows' clock is off, but FT8 Studio uses the exact time (measured with time servers) for its turns, to transmit on time and for the time of FT8 QSOs. Windows' clock is not touched.
ft8.seq_manual: You picked a message by hand: the sequencer hands control back (it keeps sending what you chose).
ft8.seq_ya_acabo: That QSO was already finished (73): nothing to send.
ft8.seq_ocupado: The DX is busy with another station: transmission stopped.

ft8.seq_log_error: The QSO with {call} finished but could not be logged. Log it by hand.
settings.ft8.seq.auto: Double-click a station: call / answer it automatically
settings.ft8.seq.busy: Stop if the DX starts talking to another station
settings.ft8.seq.n_call: Times to call the DX without an answer
settings.ft8.seq.help: Double-clicking a station makes FT8 Studio call it on your next turn, repeat the call as many times as you set and, if it answers, carry on by itself: report, confirmation and 73. If the DX starts talking to another station, or does not answer after the attempts you set, it stops. Calling CQ (message 6 and “Transmit”) answers the strongest station that calls you. Choosing another message by hand hands control back. The QSO counts as done once reports are exchanged and RR73 is sent (or RR73/RRR/73 is received).
ft8.waterfall_tip: Show or hide the band waterfall (not needed to operate: double-clicking the list is enough). It is remembered.
ft8.tx_tip: Double-click a station in the list: the DX, its report (what you receive from it), the opposite turn to its own, the frequency and the message that comes next are filled in. “Transmit” arms the ticked message: it goes out on every turn of the chosen kind (even or odd) until you press “Stop TX”. Changing the message or the DX takes effect on the next turn. The turn in which you transmit is not decoded. PTT and its delay are those of Settings → Radio / CAT, and the audio output that of Digital Modes. Compound callsigns (PJ4/K1ABC) cannot be sent yet.

settings.ft8.av.help: Tick what you want FT8 Studio to point out while decoding. “Highlight” paints the line with your colours; “Pop-up” shows a small notice; “Sound” beeps. “New when” decides whether what you already worked counts on any band, only on this band, or only on this band and mode (compared with your log). Zones and prefix come from the callsign's country; the locator from the message (if it has one). If one message matches several types, the line takes the colour of the first one in the list.

settings.desc.rtty: RTTY Studio settings you only touch once. What changes each session (mode, Reverse, AFC, ATC, tone, squelch and waterfall) is in the window itself; sound cards are in Digital Modes; the PTT is in Radio / CAT.
settings.rtty.mode_note: The window's mode (45.45 baud · 170 Hz, 50 baud…) sets these two values. Here you can type your own for unusual signals: the window will switch to «Custom».
settings.ptt.test_confirm: This will put the radio in TRANSMIT for 1 second. Do you want to test the PTT?
settings.ptt.test_done: Test done: the PTT has been released.
settings.ptt.help: Radio output: the serial port RadioLog uses to key the radio and to set the PTT. It is a SINGLE one for the whole suite (CW, RTTY and the Studios to come): choose it here once. On the FTDX10: the «Standard COM Port» (the «Enhanced» is for CAT) and, in the radio menu, «RPTT SELECT» = RTS. PTT method: «By serial port» raises the RTS or DTR line of the port, as other digital mode programs do; «By CAT» sends the transmit command over CAT (the radio must be connected). CW uses the same port for the key (the DTR or RTS line is chosen in CW Studio). The Studios share the port: you do not need to disconnect one to use another. The delays are for digital-mode transmission: «before» is the wait between setting the PTT and sending the audio (the radio needs a moment to switch to transmit; 150 ms by default) and «when finished» the wait between the end of the audio and releasing the PTT (so the end is not cut; 100 ms). For safety the PTT is released on close, on disconnect and after the maximum time. The «Test PTT» button is for you to press: it transmits for 1 second.
ptt.err_sin_cat: The radio is not connected over CAT.

rtty.out_tip: Audio output: where the RTTY generated by RadioLog goes (the radio's sound card: «Speakers (USB AUDIO CODEC)»). «Test audio» sends about 3 s of «RYRYRY…» with the window's centre tone, shift and sense (Reverse), and it does NOT key the PTT: the radio does not go on the air. Check first: no VOX / DATA VOX on the radio. The volume is what the program generates; the level that reaches the radio is set with the Windows mixer and the radio's «USB MOD LEVEL». Start low. The meter shows what the program sends to the card, not what the radio receives.

cwdec.tx_conn_tip: The serial port, line (DTR or RTS) and PTT for CW are chosen in Settings → CW Studio (Settings menu → CW Studio…). Here you only choose the speed: when you send a text or a macro the radio connects by itself, and it is released when this window closes. On the FTDX10 use the «Standard COM Port»: the «Enhanced» one is for CAT.
cwdec.demo_tip: Plays a sample QSO so you can see how the waterfall and the text work, with no radio or real audio.

cwdec.waterfall_tip: Click on a station's signal to decode that tone (or select its channel if it already exists). With a manual channel selected, the mouse wheel fine-tunes ±5 Hz (Shift ±1 Hz).
cwdec.rx_speed_short: Detected; type one to fix it
cwdec.squelch_tip: Minimum signal-to-noise ratio to write text. Higher = less garbage on noise but weak signals are lost; 0 = always decode.
cwdec.filter_tip: Filter width around the tone. Automatic adapts it to the speed; Narrow is more sensitive with weak signals; Wide copes better with a drifting tone.
cwdec.unknown_tip: «*» = pattern that does not exist in Morse
cwdec.auto_search_tip: Detects the active CW tones in the audio and opens a channel (with its own text, speed and tab) for each station. Useful with a wide receiver filter, where several come in at once.
cwdec.remove_tip: Closes the channel of the visible tab (its text is kept) and it will not reopen by itself at that tone for a minute.
cwdec.no_channels: No channel yet: wait for a station to be detected, or click on its signal in the waterfall to decode that tone.
cwwin.how: To transmit from the computer, without a keyer or paddles, all you need is a serial port whose DTR or RTS line reaches the radio's key input. If the radio has two USB ports (e.g. the Yaesu FTDX10: “Enhanced” for CAT and “Standard” for PTT and CW), use the one that is not taken by rig control. You must also enable CW keying on that port in the radio: on the FTDX10 it is the “PC KEYING” menu (OFF, DAKY, RTS, DTR), which must match the line chosen here; with OFF the radio goes to TX but does not hear the key and no signal is sent. “Test mode”: only the local tone sounds, nothing is transmitted.
cwwin.err_busy: Port {puerto} is in use by another program. Close it or choose another port.
cwwin.err_busy_cat: Port {puerto} is the one rig control (CAT) uses and it is already open. If your radio has two USB ports, use the other one for CW (on the Yaesu FTDX10, the “Standard COM Port”).
cwwin.ptt: Put the radio in TX (CAT PTT) while sending
cwwin.ptt_tip: Ticked: when sending text or a macro the app switches the radio's PTT on via CAT and releases it at the end. Unticked: only the port line is keyed; the radio transmits only if it is in CW with break-in (BK-IN) on. Applies immediately, also while connected.
cwdec.tx_placeholder: Type what you want to transmit here and press Send (Ctrl+Enter). Accepts <AR>, <SK>, <BT>…
cwdec.tx_not_connected: Not connected: it connects by itself when you send.
cwdec.tx_send_tip: Sends the text in the box (Ctrl+Enter). It appears in blue, interleaved with what is received.
cwdec.tx_macros_direct_tip: Checked: F1–F8 transmit at once. Unchecked: they only copy their text to the box so you can review and send it yourself. Right-click a macro to edit it.

cwmac.help: Each key F1–F8 has a name (shown on the button) and the text sent in Morse. The text can contain variables, filled in from the QSO in progress, and prosigns in angle brackets: <AR> <SK> <BT> <KN>. If you clear a text or a name, the default comes back. Text in square brackets is optional: if any data inside is missing (your name, say), that part is not sent.
cwmac.name_tip: Name: shown on the button (empty: the start of the text is used). Double-click to edit.
cwmac.edit_tip: Edit the names and texts of macros F1–F8

digital.modos.help: Write each mode as you want to see it in the menu. With the “…” button on its row you pick the program in the file explorer (its path is saved), or paste a web address (https://…) right there. You decide which program you use for each mode, and you can add as many as you like.

cwdec.tune_follow: Tune the radio when choosing a channel
cwdec.tune_tip:
When you click a station, RadioLog changes your radio's frequency (over CAT) to put it at your pitch, so your transmission goes out on its frequency. The waterfall moves: the station jumps to your pitch line.

Enter your radio's CW PITCH in «Radio pitch». It only acts with CAT connected, in CW mode and not transmitting.

In testing: if you prefer, leave it off and tune with the VFO; the «Zero beat» meter shows what is missing.
cwdec.tune_not_cw: The radio is not in CW mode: not tuning.
cwdec.tune_far: That signal is {hz} Hz from your pitch: too far to tune to in one go.
cwdec.tune_fail: The radio did not accept the frequency change.
cwdec.beat_tip:
How far the chosen station is from your radio's pitch (the «Radio pitch» above). In the centre (green zone) it sounds at your pitch: zero beat. «+» means it sounds higher than your pitch, «−» lower.

Display only: it does not move the radio. To adjust, click the station's tab (with «Tune the radio» ticked) or turn the VFO.
cwdec.tune_invert_tip:
After each tuning, RadioLog checks whether the radio moved the expected way and, if it went the wrong way, fixes it by itself and remembers it.

You can force it here if needed. It depends on the radio and its mode (CW-U / CW-L).
cwdec.tune_corrected: The radio moved the wrong way: direction corrected automatically and the radio tuned again.
cwdec.tune_unconfirmed: The tuning direction could not be confirmed: adjust it with the VFO.
cwdec.closed_tip: Channels that stop receiving (⏹) hide by themselves so the tab bar does not fill up; «Show closed» brings them back, with their text. The ✕ on each tab removes it completely.
cwdec.bank_tip: «Normal macros» and «Contest macros» are two sets of macros. It is chosen automatically: Contest when a contest is open, Normal otherwise. The one in use is shown in blue. You can change it by hand here; it goes back to automatic when you open or close a contest. The F keys in the contest window always use the Contest set.

rtty.title: RTTY Studio — Decoder and transmit
rtty.demo_tip: Plays an example RTTY contest contact so you can see how the waterfall and the text work, without a radio or real audio.
rtty.reverse_tip: Depending on the sideband of the radio and of the station, the two tones may come the other way round, and then you get nonsense text even though the signal looks fine. In "Automatic" RadioLog tries both directions and keeps the one that looks like real RTTY (at first it holds the text for a few seconds until it is sure). If you prefer, choose "Normal" or "Reversed" by hand.
rtty.tone_tip: An RTTY signal shows on the waterfall as two lines close together, about 170 Hz apart. Click or drag on the midpoint between the two lines and RTTY Studio listens there. The mouse wheel fine-tunes in 5 Hz steps (1 Hz with Shift). On the waterfall, M is mark and S is space.
rtty.idle: Press Start to listen. The sound card is chosen in Settings → Audio and sound cards.
rtty.listening_demo: Listening to a simulated test signal…
rtty.err_open: The audio input could not be opened: {detalle}
rtty.warn_silence: No audio is arriving (total silence). Check the chosen input, the volume and the Windows microphone privacy settings.
rtty.warn_clip: Input is clipping: lower the audio input level.
rtty.call_filled: Callsign {call} sent to the QSO entry
rtty.call_error: Could not send {call} to the QSO entry
rtty.tx_tip: Type here what you want to transmit, or paste the text of a macro. «Send» (F4) switches to transmit and stays transmitting: what you type goes out as you type it, until you press «Stop» (F5). «Auto» (F2) sends the text and goes back to receive by itself. What has already been sent is struck through. While you transmit, what you receive is not written (it would be your own signal).
rtty.tx_placeholder: Type here what you want to transmit and press Send (F4) or Auto (F2, or Ctrl+Enter).
rtty.tx_send_tip: Switches to transmit and stays transmitting until Stop. Key: F4.
rtty.tx_auto_tip: Sends the text and, when done, goes back to receive by itself. Key: F2.
rtty.tx_pause_tip: Pauses or resumes sending (keeps transmitting). Key: F3.
rtty.tx_stop_tip: Cuts the audio and goes back to receive at once. Key: F5.
rtty.tx_nothing: Nothing to send: type a text in the box.
rtty.tx_err_audio: The audio output could not be opened: {detalle}. It is chosen in Settings → Digital Modes.
rtty.tx_end_stopped: Transmission stopped. You are receiving again.
rtty.tx_end_time: The PTT was released by the maximum transmit time (change it in Settings → Radio / CAT).
rtty.tx_state_keep: ● TRANSMITTING · what you type goes out by itself · F5 to stop
rtty.tx_state_auto: ● TRANSMITTING · when the text ends you receive again · F5 to stop
rtty.tx_state_paused: ● Paused (PTT still on) · F3 to continue · F5 to stop
rtty.tx_no_ptt: (no PTT: only the audio goes out)
rtty.tx_fsk_warn:
The radio is in {modo} mode, the radio's own RTTY (FSK). In that mode the radio generates the tones itself and ignores the computer audio: transmitting would only send a steady carrier (a beep), not RTTY.

To transmit from RadioLog switch the radio to DATA-U (or DATA-L) with the audio over USB.

Transmit anyway?
rtty.tx_fsk_cancel: Nothing was transmitted: the radio is in its own RTTY (FSK) mode. Switch it to DATA-U or DATA-L.
rttymac.title: RTTY macros
rttymac.help: Each key Alt+1…Alt+8 has a name (what the button shows) and the text sent in RTTY. The text can use variables, filled in with the data of the current QSO: {CALL}, {MYCALL}, {RST}, {NAME}, {MYNAME}, {MYQTH}, {NR} and {EXCH}. What is in square brackets is optional: if any variable inside is empty, the whole block is skipped («[OP {MYNAME}]»). Write in CAPITALS (RTTY has no lowercase; RadioLog converts to capitals when sending). You do not need spaces at the start or the end: they are added when sending. In contests, no final «K». RTTY macros are separate from the CW ones.
rttymac.edit_tip: Edit the names and texts of the macros
rttymac.direct_tip: Checked: clicking a macro (or Alt+1…Alt+8) sends it at once and, when finished, you receive again. Unchecked: its text is only copied to the «To transmit» box so you can review it and send it yourself with F4 or F2. If you are already transmitting, the text is added at the end and goes out next. Right-click a macro to edit it.
rttymac.bank_tip: «Normal macros» and «Contest macros» are two sets of macros. It is chosen automatically: Contest when a contest is open, normal otherwise. The one in use is shown in blue. You can change it by hand here; it goes back to automatic when you open or close a contest.
rttymac.btn_empty_tip: Macro {n}: empty. Right-click to write it.
rttymac.empty: Macro {n} is empty. Right-click it to write it.
wav.open_file_tip: Opens an audio recording (WAV) and decodes it as if it were heard live. Useful for testing with a saved signal.
wav.open_file_short: Opens a WAV recording and decodes it
wav.rec_short: Saves the incoming audio to a WAV
wav.file_err: The recording could not be opened: {detalle}
wav.rec_tip: Saves the audio coming in through the sound card to a WAV file, so you can review it or send it for analysis. You can only record while listening to a sound card; recordings go to RadioLog's data folder.
wav.folder_tip: Opens the folder where recordings are saved.
rtty.preset_tip: Almost all amateur and contest RTTY is 45.45 baud with 170 Hz between the tones: that is the default. If a signal looks fine on the waterfall but the text is garbage, it may be at another speed: try the other modes or "Custom" (in Advanced settings).
rtty.advanced_tip: Here you set by hand the speed (baud) and the spacing between the two tones (shift) for unusual signals. If they do not match any in the list, the mode becomes "Custom".
rtty.uos: Return to letters after a space (UoS)
rtty.uos_tip: UoS: if a switch back to letters is lost, after a space the text returns to letters by itself instead of staying in figures. It is best left on.
rtty.squelch_tip: Squelch: text is only written when the signal is above this level over the noise, so no garbage appears when nobody is there. With "Off" it always decodes. If nothing appears with a weak signal, lower it.
rtty.afc_tip: AFC: follows small offsets or drifts of the signal (up to about 60 Hz) so you do not have to retouch the tone. While on, on the right you will see how far it has moved.
rtty.atc_tip: ATC = automatic threshold control, for distorted signals. It adjusts the level of each tone separately. It improves copy of contest stations with echo or distortion (very weak space bits) and is on by default. With a clean signal it hardly changes anything; if one particular station copies worse, try turning it off.
rtty.search_tip: Looks in the last few seconds of audio for two tones separated by the shift (the two tones of an RTTY signal) and puts the center tone there. Useful so you do not have to find the signal by eye on the waterfall. The signal has to be sounding.
rtty.search_found: Signal found: center tone at {hz} Hz.
rtty.search_none: No RTTY signal was found. Is it sounding? If it uses a different spacing between tones, change it in Advanced settings.
rtty.search_wait: Wait a few seconds of audio before searching.
rtty.wf_tip: These only change how the waterfall LOOKS; they do not affect decoding. Speed: the slower, the smoother and cleaner the picture (and the more seconds of history). Brightness: raise it if you see nothing, lower it if everything is too bright. Contrast: more contrast makes signals stand out from the background.
qso.exch_sent_tip: Contest exchange you SEND (serial number, province, zone…), besides the RST. It is saved in the QSO and written to ADIF as STX_STRING.
qso.exch_rcvd_tip: Contest exchange you RECEIVE (serial number, province, zone…), besides the RST. It is saved in the QSO and written to ADIF as SRX_STRING.
rtty.ctx_use_exch: Use «{texto}» as received RST and exchange
rtty.exch_error: Could not pass the exchange to the QSO entry.
modo.title: Contest or normal mode?
modo.text:
You are about to use {modulo}. Are you taking part in a contest?

Contest mode: what you receive and the macros go to the «Contest» module (with its own database, dupes and Cabrillo).
Normal mode: the usual contact logbook is used.
modo.badge_tip_normal: Normal mode. Click to switch to contest mode.
modo.badge_tip_contest: Contest open. Click to go to its window.
contest.field.serie_auto_tip: Numbers the sent exchange (001, 002…) and goes up by itself on every saved QSO.
contest.tip.mode: «Mode» and «Digital mode» go together: if you pick a digital mode (RTTY, PSK31, FT8…), «Mode» changes to it; if you pick SSB, CW, FM or AM, the digital mode is cleared. A QSO is never phone and digital at the same time.
contest.tip.rst: Signal report. Digital and CW: 599. Phone: 59. Pick from the list or type another value. FT8 and FT4 do not use RST: the SNR is logged.
contest.tip.exch_s: What you send besides the RST: serial number (001, 002…), province, zone… depending on the contest. With «Auto» it numbers itself and goes up on every saved QSO; without «Auto» you type it, or the fixed exchange from the contest settings is restored.
contest.tip.exch_r: What the other station sends you (number, province, zone…), as you receive it. From RTTY Studio: select the received text, right click → «Use … as received RST and exchange».
contest.tip.zone: CQ zone of the other station. It is filled in from the callsign; correct it if needed.
contest.tip.grid: Locator (grid square) of the other station, for example FN42. FT8 and FT4 only.
contest.tip.snr: Signal-to-noise ratio in dB that you send and receive (FT8 and FT4), for example -10.
contest.tip.scp: Super Check Partial: while you type a callsign, similar ones already heard in contests appear here to help you copy it correctly. Click one to use it. It needs the callsign file (Tools menu).
contest.scp_hint_idle: Type a callsign and similar ones appear here.
contest.no_contest_hint: First create or open a contest (digital or phone): the fields for each mode depend on its type.
concini.title: Contest
concini.text:
No contest is open. What do you want to do?

New contest: start one from scratch.
Open contest: continue one you already have.
Just look: see the window without creating or opening anything.
concini.no_contests: There is no saved contest yet.
radio.info: A radio connected through CAT lets RadioLog fill in the band, frequency and mode by itself, and tune the radio from the waterfall. Connect it from the main window BEFORE operating. To connect it automatically at start-up: Settings → Radio / CAT → «Connect CAT at start-up». Without a radio everything works, but you type those values by hand.
radio.hint_no_cat: The radio (CAT) is not connected: connect it so the band, frequency and mode are filled in.
cabcampos.title: Export Cabrillo: fields of each QSO
cabcampos.text: Tick the fields each QSO line carries. Every contest asks for different ones: check the rules of yours. Below you can see how a line looks with your first QSO.
cabcampos.info: Every Cabrillo QSO line always carries the frequency, mode, date, time and both callsigns. The rest depends on the contest: some ask for RST and serial number, others only the exchange (province, zone…), others also the locator or the SNR. What you tick is remembered for this contest.
reloj.info: The clock. Right-click the time to choose UTC (GMT), Zulu or local time. Hover over it to see the date. What you pick applies to every clock in the program.
